prs.title: fix: buffer stdio server writes during progress notifications
prs.reason: [llm] cluster primary: Both address the same root cause: stdio_server() creates read/write memory object streams with buffer size 0 (a rendezvous channel), which forces send() to block until the stdout_writer coroutine is ready to receive again. This stalls a handler that emits a progress notification immediately followed by its final response, since the second send() can't proceed until the first message has been picked up off the channel. (2 PRs)

clusters.pick_reason: Both PRs replace the same `field_info.annotation is not str` check in pre_parse_json with a helper that inspects Union members before deciding whether to pre-parse. #3056's _is_optional_str only special-cases `str | None`, so a follow-up would still be needed for the same corruption bug on other primitive unions like `str | int` or `str | bool`. #2032's _should_pre_parse_json generalizes the check to any Union composed solely of JSON-primitive leaf types (str, int, float, bool, NoneType), which covers the `str | None` case reported by #3056 plus those adjacent primitive-union cases in a single change.

members.author: yaowubarbara
members.reason: [llm] duplicates #2654: Both address the same root cause: stdio_server() creates read/write memory object streams with buffer size 0 (a rendezvous channel), which forces send() to block until the stdout_writer coroutine is ready to receive again. clusters.pick_reason: #2493 deletes the error-response code entirely and leaves cancel() sending nothing, relying on server.py's exception handler to just return; the peer gets no signal at all and must fall back on its own timeout to notice abandonment. #2514 replaces the same block by importing CancelledNotificationParams and emitting a proper notifications/cancelled message, which is a notification (not a response) so it still satisfies the 'no response for a cancelled request' rule while giving the peer an explicit signal on both request-timeout and caller-cancellation paths. Since both PRs touch the identical lines against the same base commit, applying #2493 after #2514 (or vice versa) would conflict; #2514's replacement covers strictly more cases (timeout and caller cancellation) than #2493's pure removal, so it should be the one kept and #2493 closed as superseded.

members.reason: [llm] cluster primary: Pickling UrlElicitationRequiredError (and MCPError subclasses generally) fails/loses data — tracked as issue #2431. Both PRs modify src/mcp/shared/exceptions.py to fix reconstruction of this exception type on unpickle, via two different mechanisms. (2 PRs)

members.cluster_pick_reason: #2555 explicitly closes #2431, ships a self-contained fix (UrlElicitationRequiredError.__reduce__ returning (self.__class__, (self._elicitations, self.message))) wired directly onto the affected class, and includes accompanying test-file changes (tests/shared/test_exceptions.py). #2478 adds a new module-level dispatcher `_restore_mcp_error` that special-cases UrlElicitationRequiredError via `.from_error()`, but the shown diff never wires this helper into any `__reduce__` method on MCPError — so its effect on pickling that class isn't demonstrated in the diff, and no test file changes are included. If both were merged, #2555's instance-level __reduce__ on UrlElicitationRequiredError would take precedence over #2478's base-class dispatch for that same class anyway, making #2478's special-case branch for it dead code.

clusters.pick_reason: #2493 deletes the error-response code entirely and leaves cancel() sending nothing, relying on server.py's exception handler to just return; the peer gets no signal at all and must fall back on its own timeout to notice abandonment. #2514 replaces the same block by importing CancelledNotificationParams and emitting a proper notifications/cancelled message, which is a notification (not a response) so it still satisfies the 'no response for a cancelled request' rule while giving the peer an explicit signal on both request-timeout and caller-cancellation paths. Since both PRs touch the identical lines against the same base commit, applying #2493 after #2514 (or vice versa) would conflict; #2514's replacement covers strictly more cases (timeout and caller cancellation) than #2493's pure removal, so it should be the one kept and #2493 closed as superseded.

members.title: fix: don't send a response for cancelled requests
members.author: Zelys-DFKH
members.reason: [llm] duplicates #2514: RequestResponder.cancel() in src/mcp/shared/session.py currently sends an inappropriate JSON-RPC error response whenever a request is cancelled (the removed `# Send an error response to indicate cancellation` block), which violates the spec rule that no response should ever be sent for a cancelled request. Both PRs delete that same block and diverge only in what (if anything) replaces it, based on the identical parent commit 243eef5ae6.

clusters.pick_reason: Both PRs touch the identical two raise sites in auth/utils.py with the same `from e` fix. #2565 makes a minimal, behavior-preserving change: it only appends `from e` and keeps the original f-string message (e.g. `f"Invalid registration response: {e}"`). #2777 additionally rewrites the exception message to a static string (`"Invalid registration response"`), dropping the interpolated `{e}` detail from the message text — an extra behavior change beyond the stated exception-chaining fix that could affect anything asserting on exact exception message content.
